newsitem.title: FINLAND: INTERVIEW-FAGERNAS RETURNING TO INVESTMENT BANKING.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-FAGERNAS RETURNING TO INVESTMENT BANKING.

text.p: Former Kansallis-Osake-Pankki director and ex-leader of KOP's investment bank Prospectus Peter Fagernas said on Wendesday he aims to make his Conventum Oy one of three large players in corporate finance in Finland.

In a telephone interview with Reuters, he said there was room for three advisers to large and medium-size companies on corporate activity in Finland -- Merita Coporate Finance, Bjorn Wahlroos' Mandatum and Conventum.
"That is our assumption," he said. "There is much activity at the moment," he addded.

When Fagernas and his partners set up Conventum last year, they planned to make it a fund specialising in bourse introductions, but the idea was shelved due to failure to raise the 400 million to 500 million markka needed, he said.

Fagernas said Conventum had applied to be approved as a financial services firm which would enable it to arrange securities issues, and hoped to be able to enter the market for equity issues in the autumn.
Debt issues on the other hand is a volume product best handled by banks, he said.
"We do think primarily about share issues and derivatives, debentures," Fagernas said.
Conventum is currently a team of five -- three owners and two employees -- and plans to double that, he said.
Merita Corporate Finance has four partners and a total headcount of 12 and Mandatum employs 14 partners and a staff of about 20 in all.
